talk.transcript: Today, we will explore the concept of biomimicry in design. Biomimicry refers to the practice of learning from nature's models and then emulating these designs to solve human problems. For example, Velcro was inspired by the way burrs stick to animal fur. Similarly, architects are now studying termite mounds to enhance energy efficiency in buildings. By observing how nature has solved complex challenges over millions of years, we can create sustainable innovations that benefit our society. This approach not only promotes ecological balance but also encourages creativity in design processes.

questions.explain: 生物模仿是從自然中學習並模仿設計的做法。

questions.q: What inspired the creation of Velcro?
questions.explain: Velcro的創造靈感來自於荨麻刺附著在動物毛皮上的方式。

questions.q: What is one benefit of biomimicry?
questions.explain: 生物模仿促進可持續創新。

questions.q: Which aspect of nature do architects study?
questions.explain: 建築師研究白蟻丘以提升建築物的能效。
